iut_type: End Product (Teraoka Seiko, already-certified product), post-certification Service UUID type change
customer_question: On a product we already certified, our BLE service currently uses a standard 16-bit SIG-defined Service UUID, but since this service isn't actually one of SIG's defined services, we're planning to switch it to a custom 128-bit UUID for productization. Does this affect our existing Bluetooth SIG certification, and would we need to file any kind of change application? Our module manufacturer couldn't answer and told us to ask SIG or a certification body directly.
question_variants: Does switching a Service UUID from 16-bit standard to 128-bit custom affect SIG certification status?
Is a change application required for this kind of UUID modification?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to change an already-certified product's BLE service identifier from a standard 16-bit UUID to a custom 128-bit UUID, and needed to understand whether this affected their existing Bluetooth SIG certification or required any formal notification, since even their module manufacturer couldn't answer the question.
plain_english_explanation: An LE profile using a 128-bit UUID is treated as a custom (proprietary) profile rather than a SIG-defined one. Since custom profiles can't be mapped to any SIG-defined Test Specification (they aren't included in any PTS release), Bluetooth SIG doesn't require custom 128-bit profiles to be explicitly declared in registration, and verification responsibility for them rests entirely with the implementing set maker rather than SIG. As a direct consequence, switching from a 16-bit standard UUID to a 128-bit custom UUID requires no certification-related action at all — no change application, no test report upload, nothing needs to be done from a Bluetooth SIG certification standpoint.
consultant_answer: A 128-bit UUID-based LE profile is treated as a custom (proprietary) profile rather than a SIG-defined one — since custom profiles aren't included in any PTS release or mapped to a SIG Test Specification, SIG doesn't require them to be declared in registration, and verification responsibility rests with you as the implementing set maker. As a result, this change requires no certification action at all on your part — no change application, no test report upload, nothing needs to be done.
decision_logic: Service UUID format changes (16-bit standard to 128-bit custom) reclassify the affected profile from SIG-defined to proprietary, removing any SIG declaration or testing obligation entirely, since proprietary profiles fall outside SIG's certification scope by definition.
final_recommendation: When a customer asks about the certification impact of changing a Service UUID type, clearly explain the SIG-defined-vs-proprietary profile distinction this change creates, and confirm that proprietary profile changes require no certification action, to resolve a question that even module manufacturers may be unable to answer.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer mistakenly believing a UUID format change requires a formal SIG change application could delay their productization timeline unnecessarily, while a customer mistakenly believing no impact exists at all (if the change actually affected a SIG-defined profile) could ship a product with an undeclared, inaccurate registration.
